fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "America's Pluto Return and Group Vampirism", "body": "Emily frames 2020 through America's Pluto return, a transit no human lifespan is long enough to see, since Pluto rules the subconscious and the unconscious shadow, personal and collective. She expects what the cheery histories leave out, from wars and slavery to forced sterilization in the 1920s, to surface as the return goes exact in 2022, and stresses that its nature is surprise: we do not yet know what is really going on. Chance widens vampirism to institutions, arguing the federal government acts as a group parasite echoing the taxation without representation story, and hopes the result is a revolution in consciousness rather than a bloody one."}, {"title": "How Vampire Folklore Maps Energy Theft", "body": "Emily traces the vampire back at least to Mesopotamia and the Babylonian precursors of the Hebrew Lilith folklore, a demonic woman who drinks the blood of children, and forward to Twilight. For two thousand years, she says, life energy was understood as blood, hence the laws about bloodlines, consuming blood and slaughter; now the question is what we may take of another person's energy and attention. The bite leaves three choices, defeating the vampire, being destroyed, or becoming one, and she ties the last to how harm gets passed on. Chance adds the older tales of nightly visits that weaken a victim until they must feed on others."}, {"title": "Joe Slate's Research on Psychic Vampires", "body": "Chance reads from Psychic Vampires by Joe Slate, a research book built on case studies, which sorts vampires into twelve types. He singles out the narcissistic vampire, with its grandiose self-importance, fragile self-esteem and lack of empathy, and admits it described his own younger behavior. Slate's list of effects on repeated victims runs from chronic fatigue and poor concentration to sleep disturbances and irritability, and Chance adds that the book finds many of the same symptoms in the vampire. Its answer, as Chance relays it, is teaching both the drained and the drainer to connect to a cosmic source Emily says cannot be bled dry."}, {"title": "Habit, Multitasking and Draining Yourself", "body": "Emily argues nothing is bad in itself, but letting social media, the news or email dictate your life out of habit hands them the time and attention that could feed what you care about, and if cosmic energy sounds too crazy, plug into nature. Chance admits gaming on his phone while working and finding his work full of mistakes, since nobody has more than 100 percent of their attention to split. That leads to what Slate calls parasitic vampirism, draining yourself. Emily describes a multi-elemental self whose mind wants busyness and body wants comfort, and suggests five or ten minutes of meditation to pull it back into unity."}, {"title": "Boundaries, Samskaras and a Five-Step Defense", "body": "Emily calls sharing energy essential; one-way taking is what throws things off balance, and you never truly have to give anyone anything, even when boundaries carry earth plane consequences. In yoga, she explains, practice burns the samskaras, the latent reactive tendencies, and she urges listeners to stand in the truth rather than believe the Pluto return's lie that the world is simply awful. Chance warns against vampirizing yourself over a lapsed routine, and in the outro he walks through a five-step technique he reads aloud: a body scan, focusing on the solar plexus, self-infusion, cosmic infusion through upturned palms, and a hand clasp that cues the whole practice."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Emily Ridout returns for her third InnerVerse appearance, this time to talk about psychic vampires, energetic drainers, parasitic self images, & other negative relationships. Most importantly, we explore how one can repair, enhance, and utilize their own cosmic energy connection to burn so brightly that no creatures of darkness can abide in the Presence.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Order of the Vampire and the Inverted Path", "body": "Chance revisits the idea of psychological warfare through a document he found from the Order of the Vampire, a subgroup of the Temple of Set that he ties to Colonel Michael Aquino, which frames cultivating energy vampire tactics as natural evolution and treats weaker people as food. He links that human livestock view to how governments see humanity and argues the Cold War never really ended. Emily answers that Satanism is an inversion of spiritual surrender, subjugating nature and natural law to dominate with individual law, and offers the image of ten hungry people and one person hoarding all the food."}, {"title": "Kings, Statheism and Serving Two Masters", "body": "Emily recounts the Old Testament passage where the tribe of Israel asks the prophet for a king because everyone else has one, and is warned they will be slaves to that ruler, a cautionary tale about handing sovereignty to anyone else. Chance notes that his mother told him the same story the night before, while introducing his word statheism. He contrasts love, which allows infinite possibilities, with fear, which constricts reality to one outcome, and concludes you cannot serve two masters, so walking away from vampires beats trying to kill them. Emily agrees that fighting vampirism with vampirism only produces a war."}, {"title": "Vampirizing the Earth and the Rise of Biocapitalism", "body": "Chance widens the lens to vampirism against nature, using the dam as his example and a side story from the game Horizon Zero Dawn about a thousand year old dam failing on a future tribe, while insisting a beaver's dam is not the same thing. Emily, living in Oregon, notes the strong local interest in river health. Chance reframes a resource as nature cut away from source, then names biocapitalism, where human life itself becomes the resource. Emily counters that nobody can be used without allowing it, yet admits unplugging from money and the internet is hard, and expects these systems to fade gradually."}, {"title": "The Piscean Age, the Vatican and Hidden Symbols", "body": "Chance argues the Vatican drove much of the Piscean age enslavement of humanity and nature, points to the pope's fish hat, and notes money moving from banks to the cloud as a sign of the shift toward air. Emily reads the cross as a symbol of power over the Earth plane, and the cross above a circle as Earth dominating solar consciousness. Chance draws on Dylan Saccoccio's Spirit World to call the Catholic takeover a solar cult rooted in Heliopolis, adds Clint Richardson's straw man reading, and warns that dogma breeds vampirism. Emily finds Sanskrit texts easier to digest than much translated scripture."}, {"title": "A Shadow Entity Sent Back to the Light", "body": "Chance shares the story he promised, about a close friend who had long felt a shadowy presence draining her energy and appearing at the edge of her vision. During a spontaneous session of heightened sensitivity together, they sensed departed family members and then something darker that kept conveying the words taken from God. Chance told it that its master does not exist, since only reality exists, and offered it a return to the light, followed by a house clearing. Emily reflects that even darkness is made of light, citing infrared cameras, and Chance closes with the hermetic view that darkness is simply the absence of light."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I've often said that ideas are energy, and whether good or bad, the thoughts we believe most strongly can have the biggest effect on how we feel.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The image of the vampire is so potent because they can actually pierce your energetic field and take, and in doing so, either kill you or turn you into a vampire.", "author": "Emily Ridout", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/15788faf-7950-405a-a0a2-8088f6bae6e2/EMILY-RIDOUT.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The real important thing to recognize, and I'll reiterate it over and over again for the rest of my life to people, is that spiritual energy is your attention span.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "When I think about vampires, like the energy vampires, I just think you can't bleed something dry that's infinite.", "author": "Emily Ridout", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/15788faf-7950-405a-a0a2-8088f6bae6e2/EMILY-RIDOUT.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If you live backwards, you're evil.
